questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I really wanted to study in Amsterdam, so that was my main criterion. But I also wanted to be able to sign up for interesting courses, which VU indeed offered!

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The exchange committee did a great job sending out e-mails before I arrived in Amsterdam, which was very nice, and I thus knew where and how to seek out the information I needed in regard to housing and university. The webpage of VU is, however, a bit confusing and it was difficult to orientate in there when needing certain information and it took some time to get used to it.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had an introduction day at VU where we had an introduction lecture with the head of the exchange team about the university and the Netherlands in general, as well as a guided tour around campus, and time to get to know the other exchange students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Options included housing at the nearby campus Uilenstede with options for housing at dorms with other exchange students, as well as other housing options in student accommodations in other parts of the city.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Dorm kitchens

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It was really nice that you could find campus housing through the host institution and I was very happy about my housing during my exchange stay, but the registration process was a bit difficult and stressful, as you had to pay a certain amount of money to get on the waitlist for a housing and then had to log in at a special day to book your final room. However, even though you were on the waitlist and had payed the deposit, you were not guaranteed the housing accommodation that you had signed up for and it was still dependent on "first come, first serve" principle.

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Registration through OnlineMobility, online learning agreement and pre-approval of courses, and then registration on VU's own webpage for registration and course which was quite easy and accessible.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The exchange committee sent us e-mails continuously throughout the registration period and before arrival in Amsterdam, which was a nice help for the whole registration process.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was able to have most of the classes I wanted and had pre-approved from UCPH. However, the university did not have that many classes (taught in English) in their psychology department (my study area), why I had to sign up for a lot of classes outside my own field. This furthermore also meant that I could not find courses in Period 6, and thus had to take more courses in the two previous periods which was a bit tight and stressful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: VU offers a lot of very interesting courses and I was so happy myself with the courses I ended up with, but I would advice you to consider more courses than you might end up having as you might not ending up with your first choice.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I really liked the courses at VU and I learned a lot throughout my study abroad.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Master's level

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching at VU was overall very similar to the teaching at UCPH but differed in the amount of presentations and assignments you had to make, and I did end up having to do presentations in all my classes as well as 1-2 assignments and finals (I had 5 courses). The structure of the semester was also very different from UCPH, which made the style of teaching different as you had to go through the curriculum in only 6 weeks before you then had exams and then starting a new period with new classes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Philosophy of Mind, Brain and Behaviour
Neurophilosophy and Psychiatry
Diversity in Organizations
Neuroethics and Society
Systematic Review and Meta-Analyses of Psychological Interventions

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend Neurophilosophy & Psychiatry as well as Neuroethics & Society, which were both really interesting and I learned a lot of perspectives on questions regarding mental illness, neuropsychological perspectives, ethics in treatment and enhancement and much more. 
Furthermore, the course Diversity in Organizations was really great and had so much interesting readings and lectures, and I learned a lot about diversity, inclusion, equity, biases and more.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The costs of public transportation was way higher than it is in Denmark which took me a bit by surprise. I, however, ended up renting a bike (which I can really recommend) and thus only used public transport when needing it or not being able to bike to my destination.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
More expensive:
- Public transportation
- Food
Less expensive:
- Housing
- Bike rent
- Sports membership

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Cultural and social activities available through ESN (Erasmus Student Network) and the Buddy Program through which events were arranged and you could go on trips internally or outside the Netherlands as well.
Athletic activities were available through the Sports Centrum which was located at campus and at the housing campus, where you got a lot of discount on a membership if you were a student at VU.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you want to experience Amsterdam and Europe, I would recommend ESN as a good way to do so.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visiting the local spots in Amsterdam, including museums (Stedelijk, Rijks, Moco, Van Gogh), markets (Noordermarkt, Leichengrach, Albert Cuijpt) as well as experiencing the canals and the inner city with the nine streets and old beautiful houses.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Amsterdam and the Netherlands in general is very similar to Denmark and Copenhagen, so I found it quite easy to adjust to life abroad. The biggest challenge was to adjust to the academic life and challenges as they differed a lot from UCPH.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Sign up for student housing (living in a dorm really helped with a lot of socializing on daily basis) and join the activities offered by ESN and the Buddy Program.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find the cultural differences that challenging. Mostly, it was the academic challenges that was most difficult to adjust to.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really liked Amsterdam a lot and the city is so beautiful. I really appreciated spending 6 months there and adjusting to their lifestyle.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Expect a lot of work to do at the university (especially if you are taking MA courses)
- Use your weekends and holidays to explore the city as well as the surrounding areas and other cities, as the Netherlands really has a lot to offer.
- Sign up for university housing - living in a dorm was a really nice way to have daily contact with other exchange students and have a community throughout your stay abroad.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: NO

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I really liked to experience of living abroad and getting to know a new city, culture, new people, a new university, and way to study, as well as getting to know people from all over the world. I would really recommend going on exchange if you are thinking about it.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Definitely the academic pressure. I loved the university and the courses I took throughout the semester, but the deadlines including many presentations and assignments was quite challenging for me to keep up with, which I was not prepared for.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
